extracted.intended_audience: news editors and wire-service journalists (AP/newspaper newsrooms)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing and editing Associated Press wire dispatches (dateline format, embargo/advance marking, bylines, editor instructions and internal routing codes) for newspaper publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Dateline should appear at start of dispatch as CITY, COUNTRY, DATE-(AP)- (examples on page: "STOCKHOLM, SWEDEN, JULY 20-(AP)-", "ATRENS, GREECE, JULY 20-(AP)-", "WASHINGTON, JULY 20-(AP)-").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place city and country in caps, then the date and the AP tag separated by a hyphen; used to locate and time-stamp the story for editors and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance/embargo marking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explicit advance/embargo markers for timed release (page examples: "(ADVANCE FOR USE AT 6 PM EASTERN STANDARD TIME THURSDAY JULY 20--EDITORS NOTE DATE)", "(END ADVANCE FOR USE AT 6 PM EASTERN STANDARD TIME THURSDAY JULY 20)").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark start and end of advance material clearly; include exact release time zone and date and an 'EDITORS NOTE' if necessary so newsrooms honor embargoes and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' procedural instructions (insert/delete/replace)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit edit/layout directions to editors such as where to insert or eliminate paragraphs (examples: "EDITORS | WASHINGTON--INSERT SECOND NIGHT LEAD MILITARY-MANPQUER AT END OF SECOND GRAF XX SEVERAL AIR RESERVE UNITS SAID BY OFFICIALS TO TOTAL 9,000 OFFICERS AND MEN" and "ELIMINATING 16TH GRAF BEGINNING 'NOBODY HINTED AT THE EXACT NUMBERS, ETCe*'").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear markers (position, paragraph number or lead label, exact text to add/remove) so newspaper copy desks can apply piece-specific changes for different editions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline attribution and reporter credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Include reporter byline and sometimes location (examples: "BY JOHN SCALI ;", "BY ROGER DeGREENE", "BY JOHN McHIGHTOWER").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit the reporter prominently under the lead or headline; maintain consistent capitalization and placement so editors know authorship and can route queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead labels / edition and topic markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify which lead is intended and for which edition or topic (examples: "SECOND NIGHT LEAD MILITARY-MANPQUER", "NIGHT LEAD DEFENSE-GENERAL", "SECOND NIGHT LEAD MILITARY-MANPOWER").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use lead labels to indicate which paragraph should serve as the lead for specific editions (night, second night) and to mark topical focus for copy editors and layout desks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution and official sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute information to clear sources: news agency dispatch, foreign office spokesmen, papers, officials (examples: "the news agency dispatch from new york said:", "a foreign office spokesman declined to comment on this possibility.", "the paper added...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute claims and quotes to named sources (agencies, spokesmen, newspapers, officials) to preserve credibility and allow editors to judge sourcing weight and legal risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal routing/product codes and segment identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed internal product/routing codes and abbreviations for editorial systems (examples on page: "B&é (SCEG) (400) -17-", "RZ1025PED", "RZ459PED", "AL39WX (ADV)").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include established wire-service codes, segment identifiers and length/priority markers so central desks and regional feeds can route, file and paginate stories correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial packaging markers (ADV, EDITORS, END ADVANCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explicit packaging markers in copy to separate editorial instructions, advertising/advance tags and story body (examples: multiple occurrences of "(ADVANCE)", "EDITORS", and "(END ADVANCE...)" throughout the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly delimit editorial notes and packaging instructions from the body text to prevent accidental publication of internal directions; mark both the beginning and the end of packaged segments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and timeliness emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Flag time-sensitivity and scheduling considerations in copy (examples: advance release time, 'FOR USE AT 6 PM', references to congressional timing and expected legislative schedules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call out time-sensitive elements so editors prioritize and schedule publication appropriately; when a story is tied to an event or government timing, note that explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline/teaser and capitalization conventions for wire text
rubrics_metrics.description: Wire stories use distinctive capitalization/punctuation in headlines and leads (page shows all-caps datelines and section headers and hyphenated AP tags: e.g., "WASHINGTON, JULY 20-(AP)-").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow wire-house style for capitalization and punctuation to ensure consistent appearance across newspapers and feeds; keep dateline and AP tag formatting intact.
